Thanks for the ping — quick technical read below. I reviewed Acme's CSV and the redline. TL;DR: we can support a scoped "training exception" with specific guardrails, but it requires product + infra changes and a documented operational policy.

Technical notes / constraints:
- Scope: we should limit to aggregated telemetry and token-level metrics (no raw prompt storage). Any example-based training (even anonymized) creates additional risk and will require a separate workflow.
- Retention: recommend a firm 30-day max retention for telemetry used in calibration pipelines; afterwards artifacts must be deleted or moved to an auditable, access-restricted bucket.
- Access controls: training pipelines must be run in a dedicated namespace with elevated logging, RBAC, and HSM-wrapped keys. No ad-hoc downloads.
- Auditability: we need automated provenance metadata (who started the job, dataset id, intent) and immutable logs for inspections.
- Opt-out: we can honor customer-level opt-out via the existing account flag; ensure that opt-out toggles pipeline filters.

Operational impact and timeline:
- Minor infra work: ~2 sprints to add the dedicated namespace + retention enforcement hooks and provenance metadata hooks.
- Documentation + runbook for security: 1 sprint.
- Risk: increases surface area for training code; must be gated by security review and an annual penetration test.

Suggested redline language (high level):
"Redwood may use anonymized, non-personally-identifiable telemetry from the Customer's requests for internal model calibration or quality improvement subject to: (i) explicit written consent; (ii) a time-bounded retention window not to exceed thirty (30) days unless agreed otherwise; (iii) execution in an isolated processing environment with auditable provenance logs; and (iv) no use for public model releases."

I can draft more precise product-facing wording if Legal wants that. Happy to join the sync.

Thanks — I've reviewed Dev's proposal and Acme's redline. Legal is broadly open to a tightly scoped carve-out with the following binding conditions we would propose back to Acme: 

1) Purpose & scope: insert a clause that limits usage strictly to internal, non-commercial model calibration intended only to improve service stability and per-account quality metrics. No new product features or public model release without separate written agreement.
2) Retention & deletion: 30-day maximum retention for artifacts used in calibration unless Customer provides explicit, documented consent for longer.
3) Auditability & attestations: Redwood will maintain immutable provenance logs of any training jobs and provide an audit report upon Customer request (reasonable frequency).
4) Data minimization: only anonymized, aggregated telemetry listed in the attached CSV may be used. Explicitly exclude raw prompt storage that contains potential PII.
5) Security controls: training must occur in an isolated namespace with RBAC, HSM-backed key material, and documented runbook. Redwood to provide a one-time security attestation prior to first use.
6) Termination & remedy: Customer can revoke the exception with 30 days' notice; Redwood will delete related artifacts within 30 days and provide deletion confirmation.

I attached a short tracked-changes doc (REDCAP_Product_Security_Notes.docx) that maps Dev's operational asks to legal language. If Product and Security confirm the implementation timeline (2 sprints + runbook + attestation), I'm comfortable advancing this conditional carve-out to Acme.

Next steps for the thread:
- Dev: confirm sprint commitment and whether the namespace + provenance hooks can be completed in the timeline.
- Hannah: confirm what form the "one-time security attestation" would take and whether we need a supporting pen-test before we sign.
- Priya: if all agree, I'll send a redlined DPA back to Acme and propose an addendum with the technical appendix referenced.
